questions.q: What is the best basic definition of a **Constitution**?
options: A religious book used strictly for taking oaths in court
A body of fundamental rules, laws, and principles by which a state or organization is governed
A confidential document revealing a nation's military secrets
An agreement strictly between opposing political parties during elections
questions.explain: A **Constitution** is defined as the whole body of fundamental laws, customs, conventions, and principles according to which a particular country or organization is governed.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Which of the following was the first formally recognized Colonial Constitution enacted for Nigeria, established in the year 1922?
questions.explain: The **Clifford Constitution of 1922** (named after Governor Sir Hugh Clifford) was the first formal colonial constitution in Nigeria, famously introducing the elective principle.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q:
Examine the timeline of Nigerian Colonial Constitutions:

| Year | Constitution Name |
|---|---|
| 1922 | Clifford |
| 1946 | $X$ |
| 1951 | Macpherson |

Which constitution correctly replaces $X$?
questions.explain: The **Richards Constitution** was established in **1946** (promulgated by Sir Arthur Richards). It is notable for dividing Nigeria into three regions (North, East, and West) and promoting regionalism.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: In what significant way did the **Lyttleton Constitution of 1954** shape the modern structure of the Nigerian nation?
options: It fully introduced the unitary system of government to Nigeria
It established a full Federal system of government for Nigeria
It instantly granted full political independence to Nigeria
It successfully abolished all regional governments
questions.explain: The **Lyttleton Constitution of 1954** is highly historically significant because it legally established a true **Federal system of government**, formally dividing powers between the central and regional governments.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: The **Independence Constitution**, which officially ended direct British colonial rule in Nigeria, came into effect in which year?
questions.explain: The **Independence Constitution** was implemented on October 1, **1960**, marking the birth of Nigeria as a sovereign, independent state from Great Britain.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Which of the following was a major common feature of the pre-1960 **Colonial Constitutions** in Nigeria?
options: They granted universal adult suffrage to every Nigerian citizen immediately
They were drafted exclusively by completely sovereign Nigerian elected officials
They heavily centralized power in the hands of the British Governor-General
They legally abolished traditional chieftaincy institutions entirely
questions.explain: A defining feature of all colonial constitutions was the concentration of immense executive and legislative powers in the hands of the **British Governor-General**, thereby limiting local democratic autonomy.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Under the Post-1960 Constitutions, when did Nigeria legally become a Republic, replacing the British Queen as the Head of State with a Nigerian President?
questions.explain: The **1963 Republican Constitution** severed the final colonial ties with Britain, replacing the Queen with a Nigerian ceremonial President (Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe) and making the Nigerian Supreme Court the highest court of appeal.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: A massive structural shift occurred in Nigerian governance with the **1979 Constitution**. What major feature did this constitution introduce?
options: The Parliamentary system of government (Prime Minister model)
The Executive Presidential system of government (modeled after the USA)
The absolute dissolution of the Nigerian military forces
The total merging of Nigeria with neighboring West African countries
questions.explain: The **1979 Constitution** radically shifted Nigeria from a British-style Parliamentary system to an American-style **Executive Presidential system**, making the President both Head of State and Head of Government.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Which of these post-1960 Nigerian constitutions is historically associated with attempting to institutionalize a strict two-party system (SDP and NRC) during a military-to-civilian transition?
questions.explain: The **1989 Constitution** (promulgated during General Ibrahim Babangida's regime) was specifically designed for the ill-fated Third Republic and legally mandated a **two-party political system**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Which post-1960 constitution finally abolished the British Privy Council in London as Nigeria's highest court of appeal?
questions.explain: Before **1963**, the final court of appeal for Nigerians was the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in London. The **1963 Republican Constitution** established the Nigerian Supreme Court as the final appellate authority.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q:
Identify the primary sequential order of the following major pre-independence colonial constitutions:

1. Lyttleton Constitution
2. Clifford Constitution
3. Macpherson Constitution
4. Richards Constitution
questions.explain:
The chronological sequence is:
- Clifford (1922) [2]
- Richards (1946) [4]
- Macpherson (1951) [3]
- Lyttleton (1954) [1]
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: In contrasting the Parliamentary and Presidential features of Nigerian Constitutions, what is the primary role of the Executive President created by the 1979 Constitution?
options: To act only as a ceremonial figurehead while a Prime Minister rules
To exercise full executive powers as both the Head of State and the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces
To exclusively draft and pass laws without the National Assembly
To permanently serve as the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court
questions.explain: Unlike a ceremonial President under a parliamentary system (1963), the **Executive President** (instituted in 1979) possesses full executive authority and is the **Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Which historical pre-1960 Nigerian Colonial Constitution formally institutionalized **Regionalism** by dividing the country into three distinct political regions (Northern, Western, and Eastern)?
questions.explain: The **Richards Constitution of 1946** is historically notable for legally dividing Nigeria into three administrative regions (North, East, and West), laying the early foundation for federalism.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: The **1999 Constitution** is the current supreme document guiding Nigerian democracy. Historically, this specific constitution was midwifed and promulgated by which type of administration?
options: A fully democratically elected civilian parliament
A transitional military regime preparing the nation for the Fourth Republic
An emergency coalition of traditional kings
questions.explain: The **1999 Constitution** was enacted via a military decree (Decree No. 24 of 1999) under the transitional military administration of General Abdulsalami Abubakar, seamlessly handing power to elected civilians to start the Fourth Republic.
